items.topic: Pipeline state representation for gate-blocked waiting
items.context: The pipeline state machine (types.go:37-100) has no concept of a 'waiting' or 'gate-blocked' state. When the deploy stage polls the gate, the pipeline is technically 'running' but semantically 'waiting for external approval'. The existing Poller[T] (stage_helpers.go:243-299) handles async polling but doesn't surface a distinct state to the UI/CLI. We need to decide how gate-blocked status is represented to callers.

options.label: Add a new PipelineStateGateBlocked state
options.rationale: New state in the state machine (PipelineStateGateBlocked between ExecutingStage and ProcessingResult). The orchestrator transitions to it when the deploy stage signals gate-blocked. CLI/UI can show a distinct 'Waiting for approval' status. Requires adding the state to ValidPipelineStateTransitions and IsTerminal(). Clean separation but touches the core state machine.

options.label: Use stage-level status with metadata, no new pipeline state
options.rationale: Keep pipeline in PipelineStateExecutingStage. The deploy stage's StageResult gets a new status like StatusGateBlocked (alongside StatusRunning/StatusCompleted/etc). Pipeline state machine stays unchanged. CLI/UI check the current stage's status for gate-blocked rendering. Simpler change but less visible at the pipeline level.

items.topic: Approval creation mechanism in the pipeline
items.context: Round 1 decided approvals are created automatically after build completes (d4=A). The question is the implementation mechanism. The orchestrator runs stages sequentially in runPipelineAsync() (orchestrator.go:537-749) with a loop over stages. After each stage completes, it transitions to PipelineStateProcessingResult. There's no 'between-stage hook' concept today. Options for where the approval creation code lives:

options.label: Post-stage hook in the orchestrator loop
options.rationale: Add a post-stage callback mechanism to the orchestrator. After PipelineStateProcessingResult for the build stage, fire a hook that calls dm_client.CreateApproval(). Generic enough to support future post-stage logic. But adds a new orchestration concept that only has one user today.

options.label: Approval creation as the first operation in the deploy stage
options.rationale: The deploy stage (stage_deploy.go) already runs after build. Add approval creation at the top of Execute(), right before the gate check. Keeps all approval logic in one place (deploy stage). No orchestrator changes needed. The deploy stage becomes: (1) create approvals, (2) check gate, (3) poll if blocked, (4) upload artifacts. Simple and cohesive.

options.label: Dedicated ApprovalGate stage that runs before Deploy
options.rationale: A thin stage that creates approvals and checks the gate. If gate passes, Deploy runs next. Explicit in the pipeline progression but adds a new stage (which round 1 d2 decided against).

items.topic: deploy-targets.json schema migration for new profile_id field
items.context: Round 1 decided to add a deployment_manager_profile_id field to DeployTarget (d1=A). The deploy-targets.json file has a SchemaVersion field (currently '1.0') managed by TargetRepository (targets.go:28-131). Adding a new optional field to DeployTarget is backward-compatible (existing files without the field will unmarshal with zero value). The question is whether to bump the schema version.

options.label: No schema version bump — field is optional and backward-compatible
options.rationale: The new field is optional (gate check is skipped if empty). Existing deploy-targets.json files will continue to work without modification. No migration code needed. Users add the field when they want approval gating.

options.label: Bump to 1.1 with auto-migration on load
options.rationale: Signals the schema change formally. TargetRepository.load() detects 1.0 and migrates to 1.1 (just bumps version, no data changes needed). More correct from a versioning perspective but adds migration code for what is effectively a no-op.

items.context: Round 1 decided on exponential backoff polling with configurable timeout (d3=A). The existing Poller[T] in stage_helpers.go:243-299 supports configurable poll interval and timeout. We need concrete defaults for the gate poll, plus where the configuration lives.

options.label: DeployConfig fields: GateTimeout (default 30m), GatePollInterval (default 15s), backoff cap 2m
options.rationale: Add GateTimeout and GatePollInterval to DeployConfig (types.go:227-243). Initial poll at 15s, exponential backoff with 2x multiplier capped at 2 minutes. 30-minute default timeout matches typical CI approval windows. Users can override via CLI flags --gate-timeout and --gate-poll-interval. Reuses the existing Poller[T] with these parameters.

options.label: Shorter defaults: GateTimeout 10m, GatePollInterval 10s, backoff cap 1m
options.rationale: More aggressive polling for faster feedback. Better for interactive use but creates more load on deployment-manager. 10-minute timeout may be too short for approvals that require human review.

items.text: The existing Poller[T] generic (stage_helpers.go:243-299) can be directly reused for gate polling. It supports context cancellation, configurable poll interval, and timeout. The gate check can be implemented as a Poller[ReleaseGateResponse] where the check function calls dm_client.CheckReleaseGate() and the done condition is gate.Ready == true.
